subject: ict
edition: EPD Grade 6 ICT Reading Book + Workbook (English medium, 1st print 2018, 2nd print 2019) and NIE Grade 6 ICT Teachers' Guide (effective from 2018). Pre-reform materials: the 2026 reform modules for Grade 6 were deferred to 2027 and no reformed ICT module is published on edupub.gov.lk or nie.lk.

concepts.title_en: What a Computer Is and Its Parts
outcomes: Describe the input-process-output cycle of a computer
Compare a computer with a person on speed, accuracy, reliability, consistency, storage, cost and decision-making
Name everyday devices that contain embedded computers
Sort hardware into input, output, processing, memory, storage and communication devices
concepts.guideRef: Competency 1, levels 1.1 and 1.2 (Teachers' Guide pp. 6-15); 3 periods

outcomes: Tell hardware apart from software and explain why a computer needs software
Give examples of common software such as games, media players and drawing programs
Describe how computers help in schools, banks, hospitals, factories and farming
concepts.guideRef: Competency 1, levels 1.3 and 1.4 (Teachers' Guide pp. 16-23); 2 periods

concepts.unit: Chapter 2: Use the Computer Laboratory Safely
outcomes: Follow good practices in the computer lab (no food or drink, keep it clean and tidy)
Start up and shut down a computer in the correct order
Use computers ethically and sit with a healthy posture
Explain safe disposal of electronic waste
Explain why passwords protect a computer from unauthorised use
concepts.guideRef: Competency 2, levels 2.1 and 2.2 (Teachers' Guide pp. 24-28); 2 periods

concepts.unit: Chapter 3: Operating System and File Management
outcomes: Explain that the operating system links the user, the hardware and other software
Use desktop icons to open programs, files and folders
Minimise, maximise, resize, switch between and close windows
Create, save, open, edit and close a file and organise files in folders

concepts.title_en: Application Software: Mouse, Keyboard and Drawing
concepts.unit: Chapter 4: Application Software Using Mouse and Keyboard (4.1-4.3, drawing and typing)
outcomes: Name types of application software and match tasks to them
Click, double-click, right-click and drag with the mouse
Identify letter, number and special keys and type with correct finger placement
Draw a simple picture with drawing software
concepts.guideRef: Competency 4, level 4.1 (Teachers' Guide pp. 35-44); 5 periods (1 in Term 1, 4 in Term 2)

outcomes: Name examples of audio-editing and video-editing software
Record and save a short audio clip
Put together a short video clip from images or recordings
Follow ethical rules when recording and editing other people
Break an everyday problem into an ordered series of steps
Explain what an algorithm is
Write a simple step-by-step algorithm for a daily task
Recognise the start/stop, input/output and process symbols
Draw a flowchart for a simple sequential everyday process
Turn a written algorithm into a flowchart
concepts.guideRef: Competency 5, level 5.2 (Teachers' Guide pp. 54-56); 3 periods (2 in Term 2, 1 in Term 3)

concepts.title_en: Using the Internet and Search Engines
concepts.unit: Chapter 6: Using the Internet for Collecting Information and Communication (6.1-6.4)
outcomes: Describe the Internet as a worldwide network of shared information
Use a web browser's address bar and navigation buttons
Find information on educational websites
Name several search engines and use keywords to search a topic effectively
concepts.guideRef: Competency 6, levels 6.1 and 6.2 (Teachers' Guide pp. 57-67); 8 periods

concepts.unit: Chapter 6: Using the Internet for Collecting Information and Communication (6.5)
outcomes: Keep usernames and passwords private and choose strong passwords
Use e-mail safely and recognise suspicious messages
Explain basic precautions for online transactions
Ask a trusted adult for guidance when using the Internet
